title: IFERROR: catch errors gracefully
concept:
Some formulas can't always produce an answer. Divide by a count of zero and you get `#DIV/0!`; in Level 2, a lookup that can't find its value gives `#N/A`. One error cell breaks every total that depends on it, and it looks careless in a report.

`=IFERROR(value, value_if_error)` works out the formula; if it produces **any** error, it shows the fallback instead.

A realistic case: *average units per order in a region* is total ÷ number of orders:

`=SUMIF(D2:D181,"Attica",G2:G181)/COUNTIF(D2:D181,"Attica")` is {{=SUMIF(D2:D181,"Attica",G2:G181)}} ÷ {{=COUNTIF(D2:D181,"Attica")}}.

Aegean Supplies is opening in **Epirus**, which has no orders yet, so the same formula there is 0 ÷ 0: `#DIV/0!`. Wrap it: `=IFERROR(SUMIF(…)/COUNTIF(…),0)`.

> [!warn] IFERROR hides **every** error, including real mistakes such as a typo in a range. Add it last, once the formula works, and pick a fallback that can't be mistaken for a real result: "No orders" is clearer than 0.

You'll use IFERROR constantly in Level 2 to catch lookups that find no match.

args.name: value_if_error
args.desc: what to show instead if it errors: a number, `"text"`, or a cell

worked.prompt: Average units per order in Attica, as total ÷ count, rounded to 2 decimals.
worked.explain: SUMIF gives {{=SUMIF(D2:D181,"Attica",G2:G181)}} and COUNTIF gives {{=COUNTIF(D2:D181,"Attica")}}; rounded, that's **{{=ROUND(SUMIF(D2:D181,"Attica",G2:G181)/COUNTIF(D2:D181,"Attica"),2)}}**. No IFERROR needed yet, because Attica has orders.

mistakes: Wrapping a formula in IFERROR before checking it works. You'll never see the mistake it hides.
Using 0 as the fallback when 0 could also be a real answer. Readers can't tell "none" from "zero".
Leaving out the fallback: IFERROR needs both the formula and what to show instead.

drills.ask: Average units per order in **Epirus** (no orders yet) is `SUMIF(D2:D181,"Epirus",G2:G181)/COUNTIF(D2:D181,"Epirus")`. It's loaded in the console: run it to see the error, then wrap it in IFERROR so it shows **0**.
Same formula, but show the text **"No orders"** instead of 0.
drills.hint: The fallback can be text in quotes: `"No orders"`.

drills.ask: Average units per order in **Thessaly**, rounded to **2** decimals, wrapped in IFERROR (fallback 0) so it would be safe for any region.
drills.hint: Round the division to 2 decimals, and wrap it in IFERROR.

questions.explain: G2/0 is a #DIV/0! error, so IFERROR shows the fallback text instead.
Any error at all, including ones caused by real mistakes. That's why you add it last.

questions.prompt: Why is "No orders" often a better fallback than 0?
options: 0 can be a real result, so readers can't tell "none" from "zero"
questions.explain: A fallback should be obviously different from any real result.

claimAfter: I can stop error codes spreading through a sheet with IFERROR, and choose an honest fallback.
notYet: Catching lookup errors (#N/A from VLOOKUP and XLOOKUP), IFERROR's most common use. That's Level 2.
